task: design and publish a simple website in a site builder (Wix, Squarespace, Webflow, WordPress.com, Google Sites, Carrd): choose a template, edit pages and content (text, images, sections), configure the essentials (site name, domain path), and publish; complete when the published site's live URL is shown or visited. Surface pinned: the builder session — not web-design-theory videos, not code-from-scratch HTML/CSS courses. AI site builders (Wix ADI, 10Web, one-prompt site generators) are off-task: the arc must be manual template editing and publishing.

tree.label: Design and publish a website
tree.note: Start with 1 on every route that charges or offers a free tier, then 1.8 again whenever the user sees a payment or upgrade prompt later. 2 to get an account and reach the editor; the WordPress.org routes add 2.6 and 2.7. The user goes through 3 at different points depending on the route - at 1.7 for LMVE, WfqK and sx6l, at 2.1 for FFtR, at 9.6 for Gab9 and RAex, in settings for vBcs, after 9.7 for m9LG and S7S0, and after 9.4 for Tbal. then 4 to get a starting design; on the import routes 4.8 is the moment the site goes live. then the loop: for each page the user goes through 5 for its pages, menu and sections, and then 6 for the content of each section, with 7 whenever the change should show on every page and 9.2 or 9.3 whenever the user wants to see how the site looks - Tbal loops through five pages, Gab9 through four sections of one page. The user can go through 8 at any point, usually late in the task. 9 to publish, open the live site and check it, and 9.11 sends the user back into 5, 6 or 7. the task ends at 9.8.
